title: 1995 AHSME Problem 18
statement: Two rays with common endpoint \(O\) form a \(30^\circ\) angle. Point \(A\) lies on one ray, point \(B\) on the other ray, and \(AB=1.\) The maximum possible length of \(OB\) is

solutions.text: Let \(OA=x\) and \(OB=y.\) The Law of Cosines gives \[ 1=x^2+y^2-\sqrt3xy. \] As a quadratic in \(x,\) this has discriminant \(3y^2-4(y^2-1)=4-y^2.\) A real \(x\) requires \(y\le2,\) and equality is attained when \(x=\sqrt3.\) Hence the maximum is \(2,\) and the correct answer is D.
hints: Apply the Law of Cosines to \(\triangle AOB\)
Treat the resulting relation as a quadratic in \(OA\) and require a real solution
